b: ^Kemal Aydin: He is expecting you. Go in.
^Narrator: A broad man in his late fifties, grey at the temples, stands between you and the corner office as if he were part of the wall.
^Kemal Aydin: This floor is closed. Who let you up?
^Kemal Aydin: You again. The answer has not changed.

challenge: ^The FCA. Mr Nakamoto's compliance file has my name on it.
^Dr Volkova sent me up. Ring her if you like.

c-0: ^Kemal Aydin: Do not thank me. I only open the door.

standoff_choices: ^Then step aside, or I'll move you.

on_sighted: ^Narrator: The man by the corner office turns, sees you, and steps squarely into your path.

b: ^Kemal Aydin: The FCA does not come up here.
^Kemal Aydin: I told you once. This floor is closed.

talked_past: ^Kemal Aydin: Thirty years I guarded banks for men in good suits. Then I guarded this one for a man in a hood. The paperwork is always the same.
^Kemal Aydin: Go in. I will be outside the door.
irina_vouches: ^Narrator: He holds your eye while he dials. A short exchange in German-accented English, then a longer silence on the other end.
^Kemal Aydin: She says you are expected. She has never once lied to me, so.
cover_blown: ^Kemal Aydin: Somebody on the trading floor rang the FCA an hour ago. They have never heard of you.
^Kemal Aydin: So. Who are you really?
goes_hostile: ^Kemal Aydin: I hoped you would say that.
